answer: Each identity carries a bond that only a hardware root key can move, and the node pins the TPM quote hash to the address at join. Every later registration compares its quote against the stored set, and a repeat resets both bonds to zero. An operator who wants a fleet has to buy separate machines, so a thousand seats sit at the summit of the attacker's budget before the first payout clears. The single shared jetty is the root itself, and the bond closes it: crossing this river costs hardware, not API calls.
